comment.comment:
Privacy is the next layer of crypto

Crypto promised people control over their own money. Then it put every balance, every trade and every payment on a public ledger for anyone to read.

That was a fine trade-off when crypto was an experiment. It isn't anymore.

1. Public by default is a ceiling

No fund, treasury or business wants to run its money where competitors can watch every move. No trader with size wants their entries copied before they land. No normal person wants their salary, savings and spending visible to anyone who knows their address.

A fully public chain can host speculation. It can't host an economy.

2. The demand is already here

The numbers say people want privacy, and want more of it every year: – Money held in on-chain privacy grew from $22M in 2019 to $4.6B today – The share of all ZEC kept shielded went from 6.6% to nearly 29% – Privacy protocols with real money in them went from 1 to 28
Demand didn't disappear when Tornado Cash was sanctioned in 2022. Money in privacy protocols dropped, recovered, and went on to new highs.
(Data: zeczcash.com, DeFiLlama)

3. Solana is the gap

Solana is where people actually trade. Fast blocks, cheap fees, the deepest on-chain activity in crypto.

Yet of the $4.6B held privately on-chain, Solana holds about $1.7M. Under 0.1%.

The chain with the most activity has almost none of the private money. That isn't a sign people on Solana don't care about privacy. It's a sign the infrastructure wasn't there yet.

4. The infrastructure is arriving

That's changing. @HeliusPrivacy , one of the core infrastructure teams on Solana, is building privacy into the stack itself, and @mert has been one of the loudest voices saying privacy has to be part of the base layer, not an afterthought.

When privacy lives in the infrastructure, every app can use it. That's how it goes from a niche tool to a normal feature.

5. AI raises the stakes

On Nov 25, Sam Altman announced that OpenAI is testing Private Inference with a small group of customers. His point: stronger privacy makes frontier AI useful for far more work, and "business privacy is important for a healthy ecosystem."

When the biggest AI company in the world says privacy is what unlocks the next stage, it's worth listening.

Now apply that to crypto. AI agents are starting to trade, pay and manage money on-chain. An agent with a public wallet gives away its whole strategy: every entry, every exit, every rule it follows. Anyone can copy it, front-run it or drain it.

Agents will need private rails even more than people do.

6. The thesis

The next wave of users (businesses, institutions and AI agents) won't come to a chain where everything is public.

Solana already has the speed and the liquidity. Privacy is the missing piece. The chain that makes privacy normal is the chain that gets the next wave.

Privacy is normal. Solana deserves it too.
